A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have presented a novel approach for localization of a sensor network by using an autonomous helicopter as a flying data-mule.

we have shown that a single flying node can be used to localize an outdoor WSN without any prior information on the nodes’ position, and that this method can be implemented in a distributed fashion, thus allowing the use of robotic data mule systems for WSN localization.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed method is able to localize the WSN with high accuracy, even in the presence of strong multipath effects and with only one single aerial robot.
the method can be applied to a large number of nodes with a low number of particles, which makes the method suitable for large-scale outdoor WSNs.
the proposed algorithm is robust to errors in the GPS position of the beacon-node and to errors in the measurements of the received signal strength indicator (RSSI) of the beacon-node.
